sources.citation: Datta, S. P. 2002. 'Desia (Proja)'. In: Linguistic Survey of India, Special Studies: Orissa, pp. 94ff (phonology pp. 94-97 = PDF pp. 115-118). Kolkata: Office of the Registrar General, India, Language Division.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Phonology covers vowels, contrasts, nasalization, vowel length ('Length is predictable in the monosyllabic words only'), consonants, 'Supra segmental — Nasalization: /v~/', allophones, optional /h/, diphthongs, triphthongs, clusters, then Morphology. No stress/accent/syllable-prominence statement; the only 'Stress' section in the whole volume belongs to the Sambalpuri chapter. This chapter is explicitly the description of the census mother tongue 'Proja' (118,726 speakers, 1991) = the Bodo Parja population.
